What happens to Qantas and Velocity frequent flyer points when someone dies?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 16 Nov 2026

The points don't have to be lost. Qantas: the executor or administrator can ask Qantas in writing, within 12 months of the death, to transfer the unexpired Qantas Points to one eligible family member. Qantas closes the account when told of the death and Status Credits expire. Velocity: the executor or administrator can ask Velocity to transfer the Points to another Velocity account, redeem them, or both. There's no fixed deadline, but unused Points keep expiring, so act quickly. Status and Status Credits are forfeited.

Key facts

  • Qantas: executor's written request within 12 months
  • Qantas: transfer to one eligible family member
  • Velocity: transfer or redeem; act fast, points keep expiring
  • Status and Status Credits can't be passed on

What are the steps?

  1. Find the membership numbers: check the person's cards, the airline apps, statements and emails. Note them in your own digital estate plan too.
  2. Qantas: the executor or administrator writes to Qantas asking it to transfer the deceased member's unexpired Qantas Points to one eligible family member. The request must be received within 12 months of the date of death.
  3. Qantas may ask for evidence of the death, for example the grant of probate or letters of administration, and any other information it reasonably needs.
  4. Check the recipient's Qantas account is active. Transferred points take the same expiry date as the other points in that account, and Qantas Points expire at the end of the 18th consecutive month without earning or redeeming.
  5. Qantas closes the deceased member's account once notified of the death. Status Credits can't be transferred and expire on death.
  6. Velocity: email the address for the member's status (platinum@, gold@, silver@ or red@velocityfrequentflyer.com) with their Velocity number, their full name as on the account and the death certificate.
  7. Ask Velocity to transfer the Points to another Velocity account or redeem them. Velocity's terms say executors should tell it as soon as possible because unused Points continue to expire, and the person receiving a transfer must be a Velocity member.
  8. Plan to use inherited Velocity Points. Velocity treats points received as inheritance as a Short Term Activity, which only moves the recipient's Points Expiry Date to the end of the following month if that's later than their current date.
  9. Status, Status Credits and other member benefits can't be passed on in either program.

Frequently asked questions

Can you inherit Qantas Frequent Flyer points?

Yes, through the estate. The executor or administrator can ask Qantas in writing to transfer the deceased member's unexpired points to one eligible family member, within 12 months of the death. Qantas may ask for the grant of probate or letters of administration.

Who counts as an eligible family member for Qantas?

A husband or wife, domestic or de facto partner, parent or step-parent, child (including foster and step-children), brother or sister (including half-siblings), grandparent, grandchild, son- or daughter-in-law, brother- or sister-in-law, father- or mother-in-law, uncle or aunt, nephew or niece, or first cousin.

Is there a deadline to claim frequent flyer points after a death?

Qantas: the request must be received within 12 months of the date of death. Velocity sets no fixed deadline, but its terms say unused Points continue to expire, so tell it as soon as possible.

Can Velocity points go to someone who isn't family?

Velocity's terms let executors or administrators ask for the Points to be transferred to 'another Velocity account'. Unlike Qantas's clause, that wording isn't limited to family members. The recipient must be a Velocity member.

Do status and Status Credits transfer after a death?

No. Qantas Status Credits expire on the member's death, and Velocity forfeits Status Credits, Status and other member benefits once it's notified of the death.

How do I tell Velocity a member has died?

Email the address for their status tier (platinum@, gold@, silver@ or red@velocityfrequentflyer.com) with their Velocity number, full name as on the account and the death certificate. Velocity will explain the next steps for a Points transfer.
